title: Session-based navigation proposals and edge mappings
body:
Summary:
This note collects proposals for moving the Console from a mixed breadcrumb/topbar layout toward a session-oriented left rail with compact, task-first routing. Includes wireframe writeups, edge-case mapping, accessibility considerations, and a small backlog of groomed tickets to support an incremental migration.

Context & goals:
- Problem: navigation is inconsistent across product surfaces (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), causing long discovery paths for common tasks and duplicated routes in the top nav.
- Goals: reduce click-to-target time for top 10 tasks, unify entry points for model & route management, support deep-linking for alerts/traces, preserve space for customers with many routes.
- Constraints: must work in smaller browser widths (1024px min), not break existing shared links/backlinks, minimal runtime overhead to avoid client flakiness.

Design principles:
1) Task-first: prioritize surface-level tasks (create route, deploy model, view traces) over product-level marketing pages.
2) Progressive disclosure: collapse deep items under smart groups (Models, Routes, Observability) with recurrent usage promoting items to shortcuts.
3) Session continuity: keep explorer state within user session, but allow explicit pinning for persistent context.
4) Backwards compatibility: deep links continue to resolve to routes for 12 months; logged redirects recorded for telemetry.

Proposed left rail skeleton (compact-first):
- Top area: product logo + global quick search (cmd-k)
- Primary groups (icons + 1-line labels):
  * Home (dashboard snapshots)
  * Projects (org/project switcher)
  * Models
    - Model catalog (browse)
    - Model versions
    - Upload/Import
  * Routes
    - Active routes (table view)
    - Route editor (new/edit flow)
    - Canary rollouts
  * Observability
    - Traces & latency (live)
    - Cost breakdown (token + infra)
    - Alerts (rules & incidents)
  * Deployments (Dedicated / Private)
  * Optimize (recommendations)
  * Settings (team & billing)
- Secondary area: help, keyboard shortcuts, feature flags (for internal rollout)

Routing rules & deep-link strategy:
- Canonical route id scheme: /{org}/{project}/(models|routes|observability)/:{resourceId}?view={tab}&session={sessionId}
- sessionId optional: when present restores rail expansion & table filters from the originating session. Sessions expire after 48h by default.
- Fallbacks: if resourceId missing, redirect to parent list and fire toast: "Item not found — showing all Routes" (telemetry: NAV-404).
- Redirection guard: legacy links (/routes/123/edit) are mapped by middleware to canonical path with 301 for permanent redirects; during migration we add a temporary 302 shim for 90 days.

Wireframes (write-ups, not images):
1) Route list (default compact rail):
  - Left rail collapsed to icons only (hover expands), top shows project avatar.
  - Center: sortable table with pinned filters (model, region, status).
  - Right: preview panel (selected route quick summary).
  - Key interaction: double-click row -> opens route editor in slide-over; Esc closes and returns focus to previously selected row.

2) Route editor (task flow):
  - Three-column layout on wide screens: editor form, policy/rollout preview, KV cache & metrics panel.
  - Mobile/wide narrow: form becomes primary with accordion for preview & metrics.
  - Save behavior: autosave draft every 6s; explicit Deploy button runs validation hooks.

3) Observability hub (session restore):
  - When arriving from an alert link, sessionId preserves the rail expansion to Observability -> Alerts and applies time-range + filter derived from the alert.
  - Breadcrumb replaced by compact chips showing active filters and quick-turn buttons to toggle time-window (1m, 5m, 1h, 24h).

Microinteraction notes:
- Rail hover: 180ms delay before expansion to prevent accidental open.
- Keyboard nav: arrow keys to move focus among rail icons; Enter to open primary list; / to focus search.
- Loading states: skeletons for list loads; when opening slide-over defer preview fetch until animation complete to reduce perceived jank.

Accessibility + internationalization:
- Ensure rail icons have aria-labels and role=\"navigation\" with landmark queries.
- Contrast targets for compact rail (WCAG 2.1 AA).
- Expand/collapse state persisted with localStorage keyed by org+user (opt-out via setting).
- Text truncation: use ellipsis with title attribute so long route names are readable on hover (important for non-LTR locales).

Edge cases & unresolved questions (to decide in next sync):
- Large orgs with 5000+ routes: do we move to hierarchical pagination or virtualized tree? (perf spike risk).
- Cross-project search behavior: should search always default to current project or wide-scope when cmd-k invoked with a modifier?
- Session lifetime: 48h may be too short for long-running investigations; propose experiments with 24h/7d cohorts.

Migration plan (incremental, low-risk):
Phase 0 (spike): user research + telemetry mining (2 weeks). Tickets: CONSOLE-234 (telemetry query), CONSOLE-235 (interview recruit).
Phase 1 (alpha): implement compact rail + route list slide-over behind feature flag (4 weeks). Tickets: CONSOLE-301 (rail component), CONSOLE-303 (slide-over editor).
Phase 2 (beta): session restore + deep link mapping (3 weeks). Tickets: CONSOLE-320 (session middleware), CONSOLE-322 (legacy redirect shim).
Phase 3 (rollout): A/B test 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring for NAV-404 and click-to-target KPIs (6 weeks).

Backlog grooming (short groomed items — rough estimates):
- CONSOLE-301: Build left rail component (8d) — priority: high
- CONSOLE-303: Slide-over route editor + autosave (5d) — priority: high
- CONSOLE-320: Session id middleware + restore (4d) — priority: medium
- CONSOLE-322: Legacy link redirect table & 302 shim (3d) — priority: medium
- CONSOLE-335: Accessibility audit + fixes for compact rail (2d) — priority: high
- CONSOLE-341: Telemetry event definitions for new nav metrics (2d) — priority: high

Telemetry & success metrics:
- Primary: median click-to-open-time for top 10 tasks (goal < 3 clicks)
- Secondary: reduction in duplicate route searches, NAV-404 rate below 0.05% after migrations
- Qual: session recordings and 5 post-release interviews per cohort

Decisions to capture after next sync (owners):
- Session lifetime (Priya)
- Canonical path format final approval (Marco)
- Promotion rules for frequently used items (Asha)

Meeting notes: 2024-08-21 sync with eng/product/design — agreed on compact-first approach; follow-ups assigned.

Open links and references:
- Design sketches: /drive/design/console/rail/sketches/ (see Confluence link above)
- Related: route-editor-spec-v2 (ref: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Route+Editor+Spec+v2)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep migration logs for 90 days and make opt-out easy for enterprises with strict change control.
- Consider telemetry gating so internal experiments don’t bias rollouts.
